gaps.sentence: I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.

gaps.sentence: She ___ to pass one more exam to qualify as an architect.
gaps.explanation: 'Need to' conjugates like a normal verb: she needs to pass.

gaps.sentence: The invoices ___ last week, so the delay is entirely our fault.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have + participle' criticises a past omission; passive adds 'been sent'.

gaps.sentence: Sorry I am late — I ___ to take my car to the garage this morning.
gaps.explanation: Past obligation uses 'had to', since 'must' has no past form: had to.

gaps.sentence: She is not answering her phone — she ___ have gone into the meeting, I suppose.
gaps.explanation: 'Might have' expresses a tentative explanation: might have gone.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ leave any bags unattended; security removes them at once.
gaps.explanation: 'Must not' expresses prohibition; 'need not' would mean it is optional.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay at home tonight, if that is all right.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference: would rather stay.

gaps.sentence: Tomorrow is a public holiday, so we ___ answer any emails.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' shows the action is not necessary: needn't answer.
